extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, institution administrators, and other stakeholders following NIH funding policy and process updates
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update landing page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource announcements relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes human relevance and translational potential while recognizing multiple valid approaches. Choose models that best address the scientific question rather than adopting approaches for their novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure and application format as presented in NIH’s overview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview to learn key features, the required application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare Data Management and Sharing Plans using the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format, which is based on a simplified set of required elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH issued a new format intended to simplify required elements for pilot DMS plans; applicants should follow this format when preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, awards, and related activities should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations as part of ensuring reliable biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan encourages a culture valuing replication and reproducibility and the agency has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize such efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, applications falling below a 33% cut-off had the middle third designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains a review outcome category (applications that are strong but not in the top third for discussion). Applicants receiving this designation should understand it reflects relative ranking within the study section and recent procedural modifications to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review has been centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) as of March 2025, a change intended to affect peer-review efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and administrators should be aware that review processes and structures may differ under centralized review; the change may have operational effects (e.g., assignment, study section procedures) on how applications are handled and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay current with NIH notices, resources, and schedule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscribe to NIH Extramural Nexus emails and use available resources (videos, blog posts, notices) to stay informed about updates, policy changes, and resources affecting NIH extramural research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights various resource types (news items, videos, FAQs, guidance documents) and calendar/meeting notices—regular monitoring or subscription is recommended to maintain compliance with evolving requirements and opportunities.
